subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning this as a single TypeScript module for a static vehicle model, deciding since it's not a creature it likely doesn't need joints—just basic parts and rods should suffice, though I'm considering whether a turret or barrel might warrant a joint anyway.

Now I'm working out the actual dimensions: a ~10m long carrier chassis with six wheels, a front cab, and a railgun turret mounted toward the rear with its barrel extending forward over the cab. I'm sketching out helper functions for boxes and wheels, deciding on wheel orientation and axle placement, and planning four deployable stabilizer legs extending outward from the hull corners down to ground pads.

Still positioning hull components...

Shaping the cab as an extruded wedge profile instead, defining the slanted front face with a simple polygon in the z-y plane and extruding it along the x-axis for thickness, then adding a slanted windshield slab to match.

Now designing the turret structure: a base ring, a boxy body on top, and a railgun barrel angled upward about 12°, built from parallel rails flanking a central insulator core using muzzle and breech reference points to position the geometry.

Still building railgun details...

Adding rails over the turret roof, then recoil cylinders and hydraulic buffers beneath the barrel. I'm also planning detail elements: hazard stripes on the stabilizer beams and bumper, headlights and tail lights, side vents, a rear cooling radiator, antennas, and a radar dish on the cab roof.

I'm laying out more details -- exhaust stacks, side fuel tanks, unit insignia emblems on the door, number panels, a rear ladder, towing hook, and stowage boxes -- while settling on a color palette of olive drab, tan, gunmetal, steel, black tires, yellow, cyan glow, and red accents. Now I'm working out the angled deck armor plating and cab details like the door outline, handle, and mirror.

Adding front cab details...

Adding more wheel parts, then axle rods connecting the wheels, and helper functions for boxes and cylinders to build out the hull and suspension details, plus hazard stripe markings.

Now I'm figuring out the outrigger placement at the four corners, computing wheel spans and gaps so the outrigger beams clear the wheels without colliding.

Modeling the leg geometry...

Still working out hull and deck placement dimensions...

Checking clearances, I need to keep the radar mast and dish small and offset so they don't collide with the barrel's coil bands and bottom clearance—placing the dish off-center at x=-0.8, z 3.2, with the antenna at x=1.0 to avoid overlap. That settles the turret roof details, so now I'm moving on to the turret itself.

Now I'm defining the ring cylinder, turret body box, and sloped front armor including the mantlet, side skirts, and a roof hatch with a sensor eye pod, before moving on to barrel geometry.

I'm working out the barrel's slight downward slope using a parametric function along the z-axis, then setting up tapered frustum rails extending from the breech to the muzzle.

I'm adding thin cyan glow strips running along the barrel for an accent, plus a series of alternating steel and dark reinforcement bands spaced along its length, each topped with a small glowing highlight.

Now I'm shaping the muzzle end with a thick housing block and a glowing ring around the dark bore opening, then building the breech as a wider block jutting backward from the turret with cooling fins and a counterweight on top. I'm starting on the cradle structure that will hold the barrel assembly.

Adding the elevation rod, then moving to the front details: headlights as glowing yellow-white boxes near the cab's front face, a dark grille box with bars at center, and figuring out the bumper and hull front positioning relative to the cab.

I'm adding door glass panels in dark teal, thin door seam lines, handles, and side mirrors with arm-and-box geometry. For decoration I'm placing a yellow chevron insignia on the turret and considering roundel emblems on the turret skirts—white cylinder with a red inner disc.

Now I'm shaping the radar dish as a lathe-generated cone with a tilted axis and mast rod, plus rear antennas with small glowing red beacons and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab.

Also planning towing eyes and a rear ladder with rungs near the deck, plus capacitor banks as horizontal cylinders along the deck sides with glowing cyan end caps, figuring out spacing so they fit behind the turret without overlap.

I'll skip bones for the cable paths since static models can omit joints, then add a couple more cables. For side details, I'm considering small stowage boxes along the hull sides between the wheels and outriggers, placing them at a safe z-offset away from the outrigger beam positions.

I'm placing a tan tool box with a latch at the gap behind the beams, and skipping extra rivets or panel lines for simplicity in favor of hull vents. For ground contact, I need to shrink the tire radius slightly so the tread blocks don't sink below the ground plane, keeping the wheel bottom flush at y=0.

Now I'm setting up a helper function to position parts along the hull's slanted profile using the slope direction, then planning the imports I'll actually need—THREE, the builder, Catmull curves, and a glow effect—before typing out the parts options structure.

Writing wheel geometry...

Adding fenders, support lips, and axle/differential geometry...

Now I'm adding the glass material, a hazard-stripe helper function, and the beam structures with alternating yellow/black warning stripes on top.

Still working on leg geometry, computing rod positions between joints and deciding colors for the sleeve and piston parts...

Deciding to skip the extra capsule detail and simplify instead, I'll add base lighting glow, use the rod helper with array inputs and color parameter, and the lathe helper for the dish outline. Now writing the final concise code, keeping the mirror convention where s=+1 corresponds to +X on the left side.
